Engine-independent (same on Wine 10 and our Wine 11 build).
knownIssues.fix: The game binary works: launching acs.exe directly (with steam_appid.txt = 244210, Steam running, D3DMetal) starts the sim. A launcher-bypass pin is the practical route until the .NET config init is fixed.
knownIssues.symptom: The launcher (AssettoCorsa.exe, .NET/WPF) shows 'Configuration system failed to initialize' and exits; the game itself never starts from Steam's Play.

knownIssues.cause: the game needs Steam's app identity, which Steam sets when you press Play. Without SteamAppId=244210 in the environment it quits before it initialises anything, which looks like a broken game rather than a missing variable.
knownIssues.fix: launch it from Steam, or from Highball's Play, which is what sets it. Only relevant to launching the executable by hand.
knownIssues.symptom: acs.exe exits immediately with no error and no log when started directly.

knownIssues.cause: measured from the reporter's video.ini (highball#94): SHADOW_MAP_SIZE=-1, which the launcher writes when Shadows is set to off, becomes a shadow texture of size 4294967295 on D3DMetal and Metal refuses it. Mirror and cubemap SIZE=0 are the same class of value
knownIssues.fix: confirmed by the reporter (highball#94): in the launcher's Options, Video set Shadows to Low or higher (SHADOW_MAP_SIZE 1024 or 2048 in cfg/video.ini) and give Mirrors and Reflections a size (512 here), then the session starts on a 13-inch M1 with 8 GB
knownIssues.symptom: On D3DMetal the session dies on Start with a Metal assertion, a texture of width and height 4294967295 (reported on a 13-inch M1 with 8 GB, macOS 26.6.2, highball#94)

games.notes: Works end to end with two things in place: install the .NET Framework 4.8 dependency first (bottle settings → Dependencies; took 6 minutes here on 2026-09-02, can take 20-40 and looks frozen — let it finish), and use the D3DMetal renderer. The stock launcher is a 32-bit .NET/WPF app: without .NET it dies silently, which was the long-standing 'AC won't launch' failure (re-confirmed 2026-09-02: on a bottle whose registry claimed 4.8 but only had Wine Mono, the launcher died with a Mono TypeLoadException on CEF3; after the real dotnet48 install it rendered fully). Re-verified on macOS 26.6.2, 2026-09-02, D3DMetal: launcher intro movie and main menu render, a practice session (Ferrari 458 at Laguna Seca) loads and runs at 127-128 fps at 1728x1117 (Metal HUD). On macOS 14.6 (2026-08-28) sessions ran at 150-170 fps fullscreen with a clean exit. DXMT: on macOS 14.6 it black-screened the session (engine runs, never paints); on macOS 26.6.2 (2026-09-02) the same session rendered and drove under DXMT 0.80 at 69-136 fps, so the black screen looks tied to the older OS. If you get a black screen on session start, switch the bottle to D3DMetal, stop all bottle processes, and relaunch. Launcher news panels may spin forever; cosmetic. Re-checked on 2026-10-05 on an M4 with engine r21 (DEP kept on): without .NET 4.8 the launcher dies on Mono's CEF3 load as described; the recipe installs .NET 4.8 and the launcher then opens on its language screen. No session was driven in that run.
games.provenance: verified locally on Apple Silicon (M1 Pro), engine sikarugir-10.0_6, Highball 0.7.18, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), 2026-09-02; first verified on macOS 14.6 with Highball 0.7.10, 2026-08-28. Measured driving at Laguna Seca in the Ferrari 458 cockpit, 1728x1117, D3DMetal (Game Porting Toolkit 3.0, D3D11): GPU 7.6 ms of an 8.9 ms frame with 1447 draws, so it is GPU-bound and healthy rather than CPU-starved. Measured 2026-09-10 on a fresh install with .NET Framework 4.8 installed. Reported by Dhruv9449 (highball-db#379, 2026-10-07), Apple M1 Max, macOS 27.0, Highball 0.10.10, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r21, D3DMetal with the recipe's .NET 4.8, rated 5 of 5 after 36 minutes of driving, the first driven session on r21 and macOS 27.

games.notes: Reported playable at 40-60 fps on an Apple M4 with the bottle set to D3DMetal, installed through Steam inside the bottle and launched from Highball. No workarounds, launch options or DLL overrides were needed. BeamNG probes for Direct3D 12, finds no usable device and falls back to Direct3D 11 on its own, so it does not depend on the D3D12-only path. Reported on Highball 0.7.14 with game Alpha v0.39.4, windowed at 1470x934, 6 GB reported to the game as video memory. DXMT is untested on this hardware: the earlier DXMT note came from the DXMT changelog rather than a run. A second, short report on an M5 with DXMT rates it playable, with the laptop heating up at once and story mode unable to generate a seed. On D3DMetal the game now picks DirectX 12, where the terrain does not load (highball-db#474), so Play passes -gfx dx11 to keep it on DirectX 11. Frame spikes come from the CPU side under Rosetta rather than the GPU. With more than one vehicle on the map performance drops even at the lowest settings on an M4 (highball-db#508).

games.notes: Gets in game with high frame rates once its configuration tool and the game run the same way, and the sound is broken. The game stores the graphics card's ID from BinaryDomainConfiguration.exe and refuses to start when the game sees another one. On the default engine in D3DMetal or DXVK mode a Direct3D 9 game sees the Mac's chip with an ID that stays the same from run to run, while Wine's own Direct3D and the Wine 11 engine show a different card (measured on an M4, 2026-10-05). The player added the configuration tool to the environment's programs so both run in the same mode. The CRI audio middleware loads XAudio 2.7, which the Linux fix replaces with Microsoft's own; the 'Microsoft XAudio 2.7 and XACT' dependency does that here, and on Binary Domain it did not stop the stutter (the player still hears and sees it, 0.10.9). Highball's limiter in the 0.10.15 engines did not change the stutter either, so it is not clipping (highball-db#345).

games.notes: Unreal Engine 5 first-person shooter, Direct3D 12 only, and the report ran it on D3DMetal (from 0.9.26 Play picks that for Unreal 5 builds on its own). On a base M5 the one report gets about 40 to 50 fps on the training ground and around 30 fps online with every setting low, TSR at Quality, and the render resolution at half the display's native. Playable, but the reporter's own verdict is that a shooter at 30 to 40 fps is not the experience of better hardware. The game asks to install its Unreal prerequisites at every launch; agreeing to every prompt, including the ones labelled uninstall, lets it run (0.9.25 and later adopt runtimes a game installs, which may end the repeat prompts). A second report, on an M2 MacBook Air with the Wine 11 engine, averages about 23 fps with stretches of 30 to 45, and hits a problem the first did not: gunfire sets off an audio feedback loop and the frame rate sinks gradually after it. Their audio DLL overrides were an attempt against it, not a fix. Their later edit adds the settings that ran at 800p: AMD upscaling at Quality, frame generation on, the in-game limit at 30 and global illumination on High, so the non-TSR upscaler crash seen on the M5 with engine r3 did not happen there. Lobbies held steady, matches with bots were heavier with pop-in at the start, and an 8BitDo SN30 Pro controller made turning sluggish where a mouse played better.

games.notes: Plays on macOS 26 with engine x64-crossover26.3-r7 or later and the csgo-legacy recipe: the game alone gets the engine's wined3d Direct3D 9 (a native d3d9.dll in its bin folder, taken first for csgo.exe) and an NVIDIA identity; r7 carries the 32-bit NVAPI stub the game then needs. The environment stays on DXMT, so Steam and every other game are untouched. 17 fps at 1728x1117 with the defaults on an M1 Pro, so lower the resolution or the settings. Why this route: on DXVK's Direct3D 9 the map load on macOS 26 either loses the GPU device on Source's HDR pass (highball#34) or never finishes after the console reaches INGAME, and on the Wine 10 engine it freezes in a lost wake-up; wined3d (CodeWeavers' Direct3D 9 on OpenGL, the route CrossOver users take) has none of those, and it fails Source's shadow-map check only with an AMD identity. History: NVAPI 0xFFFFFFFE with any non-AMD identity was a dead end while the stub was placed beside the game; NVIDIA's SDK loads nvapi.dll from the system directory only. After moving a bottle to r7, Repair it once so the stub's placeholder is written. On macOS 14 and 15 the game also runs on DXVK's Direct3D 9 (verified 2026-09-02 on the Wine 10 engine). Cold check 2026-09-11 on Highball 0.9.7 (M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine r7): the game deleted and downloaded again by Steam launched from Play, which put the d3d9.dll back and started it on wined3d with the NVAPI stub loaded; it held its 1728x1117 window for three minutes. No round played in that check. Re-checked on 2026-10-05 on an M4 with macOS 27.0 and the Wine 11 engine r15: with the recipe applied the game loads de_dust2 straight from +map and plays the round (console INGAME); without it, the CSM check error with the AMD identity.

knownIssues.cause: reported from the disassembly: the game calls glClearDepthf through GLEW and Wine's macOS OpenGL has no such function, so the pointer is null
knownIssues.fix: workaround by hand: Mesa's Windows opengl32.dll and libgallium_wgl.dll next to DkkStm.exe with a native,builtin override for opengl32 on that exe. Software rendering (llvmpipe), measured. Not shipped by Highball yet
knownIssues.symptom: Crashes at startup with a page fault at address zero on every graphics mode (reported on an M3, macOS 27)

games.notes: An OpenGL game. On the stock engine it crashes at startup through a null OpenGL function pointer (GLEW's glClearDepthf, a function macOS's own OpenGL does not provide). The reporter got it running by placing Mesa's Windows OpenGL build (opengl32.dll and libgallium_wgl.dll from mesa-dist-win 26.2.0) beside the game's exe with a per-exe native override for opengl32, launched through Steam with sync off. That is a hand edit Highball does not ship; it points at the same OpenGL gap as Mewgenics and at Mesa as the way to close it. Measured here on 2026-09-16: Mesa's zink driver refuses MoltenVK (no nullDescriptor), so the workaround runs on llvmpipe, software rendering on the CPU. Fine for this board game, not for anything heavier. Performance was not measured.
games.provenance: Reported by JingKritsada (highball-db#87, 2026-09-16), Apple M3, macOS 27, Highball 0.9.19, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r3, rated 5 of 5 provisionally after a workaround: the game launches, displays and responds to input, extended play and frame rate not verified. knownIssues.cause: not measured on this game. DXVK's Direct3D 9 is slow on that tree in general (highball#198's measurements).
knownIssues.fix: none confirmed. Wine's own Direct3D on r11 (the DXMT mode from Highball 0.9.38) helped, and engine r12 helped a little more, but neither made it smooth. Community performance mods are the next thing to try, untested here.
knownIssues.symptom: Under 10 fps with lag spikes in the main menu on the Wine 11 engine r11 with DXVK, and under about 15 fps (estimated) with Wine's own Direct3D there (M3 Pro, macOS 27.0, highball-db#211).

games.notes: A Direct3D 9 game from 2010. On the Wine 11 engines DXVK's Direct3D 9 runs at about half the speed the default engine's does (Five Nights at Freddy's, 40 against 76 fps, measured 2026-09-25). Wine's own Direct3D on r11 helped the reporter but did not make it playable, so the CPU side is the next suspect. Engine r12 carries the loader side of x87 acceleration only. The sidecar binary that does the work is not shipped and Highball sets no ROSETTA_X87_PATH, so r12 alone does not speed up x87 math (the Half-Life 2 figure of 131 to 174 fps was measured with that sidecar set by hand), and the reporter's r12 test measured only the single-process launch. Nothing was measured here. A later round from the same reporter (highball-db#211, 2026-09-30): on r12 the frame rate falls to unplayable within seconds of walking, indoors too. Fallout.ini changes (water shader off, present interval 0, threaded AI with two threads), windowed mode and the Steam overlay off did not help. xNVSE with New Vegas Tick Fix could not be launched, since renaming nvse_loader to the launcher sent Steam into a file validation loop, and a 32-bit DXVK d3d9.dll beside the game with a native override crashed at launch with a page fault in 32-bit code. A separate finding of 2026-10-03 (highball#165) may matter here: 32-bit programs without the NX_COMPAT flag had data execution prevention turned off under Wine, and under Rosetta that made every write into a buffer DXVK hands to Metal fault, 30 to 50 seconds per 1500 frames in a Direct3D 9 test on an M4. The Wine 11 engine keeps DEP on from revision r17, which ships with the version after 0.10.4. Not measured on this game yet; a run on r17 with DXVK is the thing to try when it is out.
games.provenance: Reported by matthiasseghers (highball-db#211, 2026-09-25), Apple M3 Pro, macOS 27.0, Highball 0.9.35, engine x64-crossover26.3-r11, DXVK, AVX advertised, rated 2 of 5: the main menu holds 40 to 50 fps and drops under 10 with lag spikes when hovering menu items. The Wine 10 engine launched worse for them. Not verified by the maintainer. Follow-up 2026-09-28 by the same reporter: DXMT mode on r11, which sends Direct3D 9 to Wine's own Direct3D (the log confirms it), starts smoother and lags less in the menu, but menu and game stay under about 15 fps by their estimate, no counter would show. Second follow-up 2026-09-29: on engine r12 it runs slightly better but still unevenly, and the reporter suspects the game needs its community performance mods to run well under Wine.

knownIssues.cause: a startup deadlock on Wine's loader lock while the game loads Steam's steamclient64.dll (after the VCLibs package lookup, fixed in engine r24), traced in highball#268

games.notes: Does not start. Steam starts the game and it hangs inside its own startup with no window. Two walls were found in turn. The first, Wine answering the game's lookup of the Visual C++ libraries package with nothing (Wine bug 55397), is fixed in the Wine 11 engines r24 and r25 (Highball 0.10.16), which register that package the way Proton does. Behind it a second one remains: inside the game a thread loads Steam's own client library (steamclient64.dll) and never releases Wine's loader lock, so the other threads wait until the game gives up; Steam's overlay off changes nothing (traced 2026-10-15). Proton on Linux does not load that library, it ships its own, which is one reason the game runs there. No Mac Wine setup is known to run it (AppleGamingWiki: does not start on CrossOver and Wine). Microsoft delisted the game from Steam in December 2024, and Highball's own test account does not own it, so the maintainer cannot reproduce it and the work goes through a player's traces (highball#268). Among Us, which works, loads the same Steam library on its main thread and is done in about three seconds; Forza loads it from a worker thread and that load never returns.
games.provenance: Reported by whcjimmy (highball#268, from 2026-10-06), Apple M1 Pro, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.10.3 to 0.10.16, Wine 11 engines r18 and r24 with D3DMetal 4 and the Forza Horizon 6 variables: the game installs and Steam starts it, but no window ever opens and it quits after a few minutes. AppleGamingWiki lists it as not starting on CrossOver and Wine. Not verified by the maintainer. With Synchronization set to None the same thread still waits forever after loading steamclient64.dll, and a macOS sample shows another of the game's threads suspended the whole time (whcjimmy, highball#268, 2026-10-18), so the engine's msync is not the cause.

knownIssues.cause: D3DMetal 4.0 beta 2 and beta 3 place vertex attributes that the game's input layouts give as D3D12_APPEND_ALIGNED_ELEMENT at the wrong offsets, so its shaders read other attributes' bytes: the livery vinyls' coverage came from texcoord data, normals and tangents were shifted, and so was the trees' wind data. knownIssues.cause: cause not established on Apple M1 Pro hardware, and a long list of candidates has been excluded by measurement on 2026-09-08 (macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r4, D3DMetal 3.0 and Apple's D3DMetal 4.0b2 from Game Porting Toolkit 4). Excluded: the DirectX 12 Agility SDK loader (the game declares SDK 611 and never calls D3D12GetInterface; supplying it changed nothing); device creation (succeeds at 12_0 on the real adapter); capability values (137 CheckFeatureSupport calls all return S_OK, and forcing every one of them to report supported changes nothing); the advertised feature level (D3DMetal claims 12_2 and even accepts device creation there, but making it report and behave exactly like vkd3d, 12_0 with E_INVALIDARG above, changes nothing); ray tracing (D3DM_SUPPORT_DXR=1 raises the tier to 1.1, no change); the GPU identity presented (vendor, device and description overridden, no change); DXGI (factory, adapter enumeration, GetDesc3, outputs, tearing, video memory budget and swapchain creation in seven configurations all succeed, identically to vkd3d); Highball's own timestamp shim (removing it entirely changes nothing); and Metal 4 mode. The game creates a device, reads capabilities, creates no resource, raises no exception, and quits. Field reports are consistent with a hardware floor: it is reported working on M4 Pro and M5 Pro and never on M1 or M2, and it uses hardware ray tracing, which Apple GPUs only have from M3 onward (this Mac reports GPU family Apple 7). That is a correlation, not a proof, and it does not explain why the same Mac starts the game under vkd3d.

knownIssues.cause: MoltenVK cannot translate two classes of the game's shaders to Metal, and one of them is a deliberate upstream limitation rather than a bug. Measured 2026-09-08 on an M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r4 with MoltenVK 1.4.1: 42 graphics pipelines fail with 'Component decoration is not supported in tessellation shaders' (84 occurrences, control and evaluation stages), and 27 compute pipelines fail with MSL compile errors on vkd3d's bindless descriptor arrays ('reinterpret_cast casts away qualifiers', 'indirection requires pointer operand'). The tessellation one is an explicit SPIRV_CROSS_THROW in SPIRV-Cross's spirv_msl.cpp, with the comment 'Technically tessellation as well, but it is too complicated to support', still present on main, so a newer MoltenVK does not fix it. Setting the game's Tessellation option to 0 cuts the graphics failures from 42 to 13 and avoids the device loss, but does not eliminate them: the game still builds tessellation pipelines for some passes. Stock MoltenVK cannot be substituted to test newer translation code, because the engine needs an x86_64 build carrying the MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT patch that lets it work behind Wine's winevulkan; upstream fat builds report no Vulkan 1.3 device and nothing starts.
knownIssues.fix: none at the app level. The tessellation half needs SPIRV-Cross to implement Component decoration for tessellation, which upstream has declined as too complicated. Turning the game's Tessellation setting to 0 reduces the failures and removes the device loss, but the run still does not complete.

games.notes: Starts under vkd3d, refuses under D3DMetal, and neither finishes. The game needs Highball's Wine 11 engine (CrossOver 26.3 base) and two graphics modes in one process tree: the Rockstar Games Launcher signs in under DXMT, the game is DirectX 12 only. Under D3DMetal it quits at once with ERR_GFX_D3D_NOD3D12, and what causes that is NOT yet known: the game creates a D3D12 device, makes 137 capability queries that all succeed, creates a DXGI factory and enumerates an adapter, and then refuses. Under vkd3d it reaches the story-mode loading screen at 53-62 fps and then loses the GPU device because MoltenVK cannot translate some of its shaders to Metal. Turn BattlEye off in the launcher first (Settings > My installed games), its driver cannot load under Wine. GTA Online is out of reach regardless. If sign-in is refused with #1.000.7, set the Mac's clock (see the rockstar recipe).

games.notes:
Story mode plays. Needs engine x64-crossover26.3-r5 or later and the DXMT renderer. Launch it from Steam: Steam starts the Rockstar Games Launcher, which signs in and hands off to the game. The row passes -nobattleye on the Steam command line, the story-mode path: without it a fresh launcher profile starts GTA5_BE.exe and BattlEye's installer asks for its kernel driver, which cannot run under Wine (seen on an M4, 2026-10-03). Checked again 2026-10-03 on an M4, macOS 27.0, engine x64-crossover26.3-r16 (the Wine 11 engine with the fixed DXMT), DXMT: the launcher signed in through the Steam entitlement and the game reached its display calibration screen five minutes after Play, nothing played past it that run.

Both of the things that used to stop this game are fixed. The launcher's sign-in window is a Chromium surface whose GPU process draws into another process's window, which rendered nothing until engine patch 0007 (cross-process child swapchains) plus DXMT_ALLOW_CROSS_PROCESS_SWAPCHAIN=1, both of which the rockstar recipe applies. And the sign-in itself was refused for reasons that looked like a network or account problem but were the Mac's clock: with the time zone set automatically, it signs in.

GTA Online cannot work. BattlEye ships with the game (a BattlEye directory and GTA5_BE.exe) and is kernel-level anti-cheat, so online is out under Wine on any tool. Story mode is the whole claim here.

Community reports of about 120 fps on an M1 Pro were measured on CrossOver's own tree, often with frame generation on. Our range overlaps at the top but the low end is 60, and the open world has not been measured at all, so treat the community figure as an upper bound rather than an expectation.

A player report on 2026-09-24 rates it perfect after 36 minutes on an M1 with macOS 27.0, on the Wine 10 engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r5 rather than the Wine 11 one this entry says the launcher needs. That has not been checked here. One possible reason is a launcher that was already signed in, since the Wine 10 engine's problem was drawing the sign-in window, but that is a guess. Re-checked on 2026-10-05 on an M4 with the Wine 11 engine r15 and -nobattleye: launcher passed, the game opens on its first-run display calibration screen. On a base M1, udance4ever measured about 25 fps in the benchmark with settings.xml set to full screen at RefreshRate 30, and about 50 fps with RefreshRate 0 and Windowed 2, borderless (highball-db#72, 2026-10-09).

The Epic copy starts through the Rockstar launcher since Highball 0.10.15, which recognizes it as GTA V and starts it the way the launcher needs for an Epic license. Two players play it that way, one with the game's benchmark at 51 to 62 fps at 1080p on a base M1 (highball-db#415, highball#309). The other, on an M4, sees the frame rate swing up and down (highball-db#463).

Two things a player on an M1 MacBook Air found. A graphics change that restarts the renderer in game (Texture Quality, or Screen Type set to Fullscreen) leaves only the top-left quarter of the picture drawn until the game restarts, so change those settings with the game closed or restart it after. And the first load into story mode can stall for many minutes while the game window is not in front, because the game pauses itself without focus, so keep it in front or turn Pause Game On Focus Loss off. A DualSense or other PlayStation controller does not work in the game's menus, while an Xbox controller or a pad in XInput mode does (highball-db#72, #415). The M4 player's frame rate swings show in the Metal HUD's graph while play feels smooth at 50 to 60 fps in 1080p borderless. Exclusive fullscreen did not capture the mouse for them, and vehicle smoke showed purple lines on Very High that went away on High (highball-db#463). A player on an M2 Max sometimes sees the lighting turn far too bright, which a restart of the game fixes (highball-db#452). A player on an M3 Max with the Wine 11 engine r27 drove around for 46 minutes and saw weird texture artifacts, not described further (highball-db#622).

games.notes:
Plays on Wine's own Direct3D, the mode this page picks: here it is about twice as fast as DXVK's Direct3D 9 (below). A fresh install starts on the game's DirectX 8 path on a Mac, whatever the mode, because this build ships no table of graphics cards. The optional fix on the game's page (Advanced, Half-Life 2 DirectX 9 path) moves it to the DirectX 9 path, with HDR lighting and better water and shaders, for about a fifth of the frame rate: 65 fps against 52 in the game's own benchmark on an M4 (2026-10-07). The first reporter played on DXVK (engine r3) and saw frame drops on shots, blood and muzzle flashes, which matches DXVK compiling each effect the first time it appears with async compilation off. Measured here with the demo, a 35-second timedemo of the opening at 1280x720 windowed with -dxlevel 95: 14 to 17 fps on DXVK's Direct3D 9 and 33 on Wine's own Direct3D, with the GPU idle at 2 to 3 ms a frame, so the cost is the Direct3D 9 translation on the CPU under Rosetta, not the graphics. -dxlevel 95 as a launch option also forces the DirectX 9 path, but Source resets the video settings on every start that carries it. The game's own -vulkan switch cannot create a device on a Mac. The r5 engine's newer Direct3D 9 layer loses the device on this game.

Measured on the demo build here: on the default engine (x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r7) Wine's own Direct3D runs the trainstation intro timedemo at 38 fps and DXVK's Direct3D 9 at 17, so the mode for this game on that engine is Wine's own Direct3D, and this entry recommends it. Both wined3d backends give the same 38 (OpenGL and Vulkan, switched through the registry and confirmed in the log). On the Wine 11 tree the same demo runs at 131 fps on Wine's own Direct3D, which is not yet understood, and DXVK's Direct3D 9 does not start there at all, every memory mapping fails on that tree's MoltenVK 1.4.2 (highball#198). A test build with athei's x87 sidecar attached adds a further 30 percent (174 fps) and is not shipped.

A report on an M3 Max (engine r28, DXMT environment, the game's own mode not stated) rates it 4 of 5 for minor stuttering over 8 minutes.

GameGuard runs in user mode and CrossOver users play online through it; every game patch can break that until the next one. 135 GB on disk. games.notes: Unreal Engine 4, DirectX 11. Use D3DMetal, set by the recipe. On DXMT the game dies at start with an Unreal fatal error, CreateTexture2D failed with E_FAIL for a 1000x1000 R8G8 texture flagged D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED, which DXMT cannot create. On DXVK it reaches the menu but the reporter found the game far too dark to play. On D3DMetal the maintainer ran the free demo (Steam 1773210) through the menus, character creation and the spawn picker with lit 3D backdrops at 45 to 57 fps fullscreen at 1728x1117 on an M1 Pro; gameplay past the spawn is not measured here yet. On engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r6 (D3DMetal from GPTK 4.0 beta 2, macOS 27 only) the demo's menu ran stable for three minutes at about a fifth to a half of r5's resident memory (260 to 700 MB against 1.26 GB) with the same GPU load; measured blind on 2026-09-19 (session locked: process, GPU load and logs, no captures), so the picture itself is not confirmed yet. Frame generation (engine r7 or later, off by default) was measured on it here on 2026-09-22, M1 Pro, macOS 27, D3DMetal at 1728x1117 on a 120 Hz display: the same spot in gameplay presents about 47 fps with it off and 63 to 74 at 2x, and it felt smooth to play, moving around.

knownIssues.cause: Wine did not mirror TEB->Tib.FiberData into the macOS %gs block, so GetCurrentFiber() returned a host value (0x8ff, which is the thread's pthread QoS class) and SwitchToFiber dereferenced it, faulting at 0x907. Measured on engine x64-crossover26.3-r4 and reproduced without the game by a 20-line test program that crashes at the same address, with the same register, on the same instruction.
knownIssues.fix: Use engine x64-crossover26.3-r5 or later, which carries patch 0008. On r4 and earlier there is no workaround.
knownIssues.symptom: Crashes on "Play Game" from the splash screen, with Wine's "has encountered a serious problem" dialog, on D3DMetal.

games.notes:
Playable on the r5 engine, which carries the fix. DirectX 12 only: on DXMT it stops at "No suitable D3D12 adapter found" before the splash, so D3DMetal is the only mode that reaches the game, and Highball asks for Apple's licence at the first launch. Reached gameplay twice from a clean start on 2026-09-09: 27.5 fps at 1280x720 in the opening scene, 17-32 fps in play, and about 10 fps for the first minute while shaders compile. The Metal HUD reports GPU time of 12.9 ms against a 36.4 ms frame interval, so it is CPU-bound rather than GPU-bound, which is what Rosetta plus 3080 draws and 3049 ExecuteIndirect calls per frame costs. A dialog saying "Your graphics card driver is older than supported" appears before the game starts; answer Yes. CodeWeavers' own testers report the same prompt, so it is expected here and not a sign of a broken install.

On engines before r5 the game renders its splash and menu and then crashes on Play Game. That crash was an unhandled page fault reading 0x907 inside SwitchToFiber, which was handed 0x8ff instead of a fiber pointer. The cause was in Wine, not the game: on macOS the %gs base is the host thread block rather than the TEB, and Wine mirrors only some TEB fields into it. Tib.FiberData was not mirrored, so GetCurrentFiber(), a compiler intrinsic that reads that slot directly and cannot be intercepted, returned the host value 0x8ff, which the game's job system passed straight back to SwitchToFiber. Highball's engine patch 0008 keeps the mirror in step at the three places kernelbase changes the field. An earlier version of this entry blamed D3DMetal's missing DirectX 12 timestamp queries and named Highball's timestamp shim as the fix; that was wrong and is retracted. The shim was loaded and active during a reproduction of the crash and changed nothing. Re-verified on engine x64-crossover26.3-r8 on 2026-09-13 (M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, Highball 0.9.9, D3DMetal): launcher, Play Game, the opening bedroom scene under keyboard control at 41 to 42 fps, 1280x720 windowed, GPU 10.7 ms, no fault. r8 replaces the r5 fiber mirror with a slot swap (the mirror hung Metaphor: ReFantazio), and this game still plays on it. The recipe keeps asking for r5, the engine it was first verified on; any later CrossOver-tree engine works too.

A player on a base M5 with the Wine 11 engine r27 and D3DMetal rates it perfect after 9 minutes, around 50 fps with the low preset, anisotropic filtering at 2x and textures on high (highball-db#624).

games.notes: DirectX 11, Denuvo on the full game. Needs engine x64-crossover26.3-r8 or later: on every earlier engine the game does not reach play, and no setting changes that. Measured with the demo on r8, DXMT, 1728x1117: language and brightness prompts, the opening cutscenes, the title menu, New Game, the naming and difficulty prompts, the first dialogue and the run through the Tradia Desert prologue, 55 to 59 fps throughout by the Metal HUD, GPU 1.5 ms in cutscenes and 10 to 12 ms in the desert, no fault in 35 minutes. The first battle was not reached in that session. Why earlier engines fail, measured: on the Wine 10 engine (Sikarugir, r0 to r2) the game faults seconds after launch reading address 0x20FF in its own code, right after creating fibers and switching to one; on macOS the slot a game reads as its current fiber is the host thread's QoS class. Same crash with AVX advertised and on DXVK, so neither the CPU feature nor the graphics layer is involved. On the Wine 11 engines r5 to r7, which mirror the fiber pointer into that slot, the game opens a black window and hangs at full CPU: the mirrored pointer is what macOS's dispatch library reads as a QoS class on the main thread, and it faults on it. r8 swaps the slot between the two owners at every crossing between game code and Wine. Keyboard: Return confirms, Escape opens the pause menu with Skip for cutscenes, F fast-forwards dialogue. The Yes/No prompts default to No, so press Up before Return.

games.notes: The Steam copy depends on EA's launcher: Steam runs the EA app installer before the game. On the default engine that installer rolls back at its last step: the EA app's setup moves its files into a versioned folder and leaves a directory link in their place, the prebuilt Wine 10 reports the link as made without making it, and the background service then cannot be found (INST-14-1627 here, INST-14-1603 for the reporter). On the Wine 11 engine the same installer completes and the EA app opens on its sign-in window (measured on an M4 on 2026-10-05), so the recipe asks for that engine and installs the EA app first. games.notes: Plays on D3DMetal. Tested 2026-09-10 on an M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2: a fight renders and plays correctly at 1920x1080 on D3DMetal, which is what this row now tells Highball to pick. The other two modes do not work for this game and the difference is stark: on DXMT 0.80 the movie, title and menus are fine but in a fight the frame flashes black most of the time with brief moments of the correct image, at a steady 30 fps and 13 ms of GPU; on DXVK 1.10.4 the 2D HUD draws and the 3D world never appears, with a clean log. D3DMetal is Apple's Game Porting Toolkit and is gated on Apple's licence, which Highball asks you to accept the first time a game needs it. Before the first start Steam shows a Bandai Namco licence agreement inside its own window that has to be accepted once. The game is built for a pad and shows pad glyphs: on a keyboard the default mapping is A = L, B = ;, X = K, Y = O, Start = Enter, movement on WASD, so the Press A title screen and the first-run save dialog both want L. Change it in Options > Controls or in config.ini next to the exe. 30 fps is the game's own cap in menus and cinematics.

games.notes: Capcom's RE Engine, DirectX 12. On an M1 Pro it stops with an unsupported graphics card error, because D3DMetal answers no to the game's check for 64-bit atomics on descriptor heap resources (D3D12 OPTIONS11), the same check that blocks Kunitsu-Gami. A player got it running, through its benchmark at 32 fps, by patching D3DMetal itself so the check says yes. Highball cannot ship a modified D3DMetal, so out of the box it does not start on an M1. On an M4 D3DMetal 3 already answers yes (measured here 2026-10-14 with a probe). On Highball's Wine 11 engine r25 (0.10.16) the variable HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 makes Highball's DirectX 12 layer answer yes, and the demo reaches gameplay on the M1 Pro with the original D3DMetal (confirmed by the reporter, highball-db#450). The recipe sets both; the game's benchmark has its own page. PRAGMATA SKETCHBOOK's demo stops at the same check and ran with the same D3DMetal patch (highball-db#485).

knownIssues.cause: The game mixes its music above full scale (the title music goes over in 25 of every 30 seconds, measured on an M4). Windows' audio engine limits such peaks, and Wine on a Mac clipped them
knownIssues.fix: The Wine 11 engine r23, or r22 for D3DMetal 4, carries Highball's limiter from Highball 0.10.15. Pick it on the environment's Full page under Advanced, Engine. On r23 the reporter still hears the music as too loud (highball-db#349), not compared with Windows yet
knownIssues.symptom: Loud parts of the music sound harsh, like a bad bitrate

games.notes: Plays on the Wine 11 engine r21 or later, which Play offers by itself since Highball 0.10.12. The game is built on the Loom engine (SDL and OpenGL, 2017), so the graphics mode setting does not apply to it. On older engines it crashed a second after start, because macOS's old-style OpenGL 2.1 context lacks a function the game loads (glClearDepthf), and engine patch 0021 in r21 answers it. The game also mixes its music louder than full scale. Windows' audio engine turns such peaks down before the speakers, while Wine on a Mac clipped them, which made loud parts sound like a bad bitrate. The Wine 11 engines r22 and r23 (Highball 0.10.15) add a limiter that does what Windows does. On r23 the reporter still hears the music as too loud (highball-db#349), not yet compared with Windows.

games.notes:
Works under DXVK with HDR on, as on Windows, and the Portal 2 recipe sets it up. Source's HDR path draws its auto-exposure occlusion queries into a render pass with no attachments, which made the Mac's GPU lose the device, so every map load froze or crashed while menus looked fine. For a month the recipe turned HDR off (mat_hdr_level 0), at the cost of Source's HDR lighting, bloom and haze. From Highball 0.10.14 it sets mat_tonemapping_occlusion_use_stencil 1 instead, Source's own switch that runs that pass on the stencil buffer, and HDR loads and plays. Checked with nine map loads across four maps on an M4 with macOS 27.0, portals included. Players who applied the recipe before get HDR back with Re-apply the Portal 2 fix on the game's page. Keep the bottle on DXVK. With HDR off, the intro map ran at 138-147 fps at 1728x1117 on an M1 Pro (macOS 26.6.2, DXVK, async off).

Dynamic shadows (sunlight through the blinds, lamps, the shadows furniture and objects cast) are missing with the defaults. Portal 2's renderer only turns on shadow maps when the graphics card reports an NVIDIA, AMD or Intel vendor ID, and the Direct3D 9 every engine uses reports Apple's. The row passes -force_vendor_id 0x1002 -force_device_id 0x73BF on Play, Portal 2's own switch for its GPU identity, so the game takes its AMD path and draws them. Half-Life 2's renderer has the same check, and with Apple's ID its console shows its flashlight shadows turned off (M4, 2026-10-07), so other Source games probably lose them the same way.

Texture detail: Portal 2 picks its lowest Model / Texture Detail on its first start because Wine reports 0xFFFFFFFF bytes of video memory through WMI and the game reads that as -1. The recipe has Wine report 2047 MB to portal2.exe, and the game then picks High (checked on an M4, 2026-10-06). With HDR on and without the stencil switch, the map loaded to a white screen on the M4 (2026-10-06).

games.notes: Capcom's RE Engine, DirectX 12 only, so it needs D3DMetal (DXMT translates Direct3D 11 and is rightly refused). On an M1 Pro the game stops at its graphics check because D3DMetal answers no to 64-bit atomics on descriptor heap resources (D3D12 OPTIONS11), the same check as the Onimusha: Way of the Sword demo and Kunitsu-Gami. A player patched that answer inside D3DMetal and reached gameplay and combat at 20 to 60 fps, which says the game does not need the feature to draw. Highball cannot ship a modified D3DMetal. On an M4 D3DMetal 3 already answers yes (measured here 2026-10-14 with a probe), so newer chips may pass the check as they are. On Highball's Wine 11 engine r25 (0.10.16) the variable HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 makes Highball's DirectX 12 layer answer yes, and the demo reaches gameplay on the M1 Pro with the original D3DMetal (confirmed by the reporter, highball-db#485). The recipe sets both. An earlier report (M4, macOS 15.7, engine r6) crashed at thread start on D3DMetal; it predates every current engine.

The installer reads it right after it measures the display and treats it as a failure. Rockstar's own log shows 'Last error: 22725120 (unknown error)'.

knownIssues.cause: found by a player (crêpe on Discord, 2026-10-13). The environment's user registry had HKCU\Software\Wow6432Node keys, left by an early Wine 11 engine's first boot when it was moved off the Wine 10 engine (r7, 2026-09-29). Wine then sends a 32-bit lookup of HKCU\Software into that subtree, which Windows never does, so the launcher's lookup of Steam's keys under HKCU\Software\Valve found nothing and it decided Steam was not running. Reproduced on engines r26 and r23. The M4 test environments never had the subtree, which is why it did not reproduce there
knownIssues.fix: Highball 0.10.16 links the key itself (gin fcee4f6). On the first launch after the environment stops it adds a registry link from HKCU\Software\Wow6432Node\Valve to HKCU\Software\Valve, the player's own fix, which they confirmed gets the launcher to its sign-in window

games.notes: Plays on engine x64-crossover26.3-r6 or later. The game uses its own Vulkan renderer (through MoltenVK), so the graphics mode setting does not apply to it; keep DXMT for the Rockstar launcher, which needs it. What r6 changes: MoltenVK refused the linear-tiled 3D, mipmapped and array images the game creates (Metal cannot back those with linear memory) and RDR2 exited at 98 per cent of its first load on every earlier engine; Highball's MoltenVK now creates such images with optimal tiling instead, and the game loads in about a minute, reaches its main menu and plays. Tested at 1280x720 windowed (Settings/system.xml under Documents/Rockstar Games/Red Dead Redemption 2, <screenWidth>, <screenHeight>, <windowed value="1" />); fullscreen at the display's resolution is untested. Wine leaves the Mac display at its own size when a game asks for a fullscreen mode; the game page's Advanced panel has Emulate display mode changes, which makes Wine scale such a game to the screen (highball#72). About 34 fps in the prologue snow with the game's Safe preset. Keyboard note: the first key after the window regains focus is ignored by the game, press it again. History, for anyone chasing the other renderer: DirectX 12 through D3DMetal initialises and then faults inside D3DMetal about 30 seconds in (execute fault at 0x20019008070c10 after 'Not implemented'), and <API>kSettingAPI_DX11</API> from some guides does nothing because RDR2 has no Direct3D 11 renderer (it falls back to Vulkan). CodeWeavers' MoltenVK 1.2.10 fork reaches 84 per cent then hits the game's own out-of-memory dialog (1729 host-coherent refusals). All of that is closed by the r6 MoltenVK. Honest playability note (2026-09-12, M1 Pro): the ride reads 40 fps on the Metal HUD but the GPU line sits near 49 ms a frame and the image judders; it runs, it is not comfortable to play here. The Rockstar Social Club overlay (SocialClubHelper.exe, GPU and renderer processes) used about three quarters of a core beside the game. A newer chip has a different GPU budget; reports wanted. Lead, not verified (2026-09-12): in Settings/system.xml, vSync 0 and fsr2Index 2 (FSR 2 balanced) cut the GPU time in the opening cutscenes from about 49 ms to 14 ms and freed the counter from its 39.9 pin; the ride was not re-measured because that run ended in a winevulkan assert (vkGetPipelineCacheData thunk, exit code 3, once in 14 runs here). The Rockstar Social Club overlay's helper processes used about 45 percent of a core beside the game. Measured 2026-09-12 (M1 Pro 16 GB, 0.9.7, r7, MoltenVK frame statistics and vm_stat): the prologue ride decays from about 30 fps to under 20 within a minute because the game's footprint reaches 13.7 GB and macOS starts swapping (free memory under 100 MB, swap-outs of up to 1 GB every 5 s); the GPU is the second wall at 31 ms a frame at 720p with FSR 2 balanced in the snow. Textures Medium, vSync off and FSR 2 balanced help the menus and cutscenes but not the ride. Killing the Social Club overlay helpers frees about a core and does not quit the game. On 16 GB this game is not comfortable; a 24 GB or larger Mac removes the memory wall, reports wanted. Verified with the Steam copy only. The Epic copy launches through a stand-in for Epic's launcher from Highball 0.9.12 and reached the main menu on an M5 Max with the vulkan-1.dll step in knownIssues (reported, highball#93). Epic copy on an M5 Max with 128 GB (reported by danekkalivoda, highball#93, 2026-09-15, engine r8, Highball 0.9.12): a stable 60 fps capped by VSync at 60 Hz in gameplay, borderless at 2880x1620, FSR 2 Quality, Ultra textures, 16x anisotropic, mostly High with reflections, water and volumetrics at Medium. An Xbox controller works. Trees near the player pop in and out at that frame rate; the reporter expects MVK_CONFIG_USE_MTLHEAP=0 as an environment variable to fix it, not yet confirmed. Two things found on 2026-10-02 (highball-db#272). Highball 0.10.2 moved a new player to engine r7, the revision this recipe names, instead of the newest Wine 11 revision, so r7 is what most players of 0.10.2 are on; 0.10.3 offers the newest revision instead. And on engines r11 to r14 the Rockstar Games Launcher installer stops at once with 'make sure all instances of the Rockstar Games Launcher have been closed', on Steam's first run of the game and on Highball's own Rockstar recipe alike, so the launcher never gets installed there; engine r15 fixes that. On r7 the whole chain works here, provided the launcher is installed through Highball (Add games, Rockstar) before the first Play. Frame rate from the 2026-09-12 run on an M1 Pro (engine r6, macOS 26.6.2): about 40 by the counter on the prologue blizzard ride at 1280x720 windowed, but uneven: GPU near 49 ms a frame on the ride, visibly juddery, not what the maintainer would call playable on an M1 Pro (third run 2026-09-12, 0.9.7, engine r7); 55-60 in the menus and the intro montage, 35 in the opening cutscene Steam, Rockstar launcher signs in, first-run prompts (brightness, subtitles, audio), main menu, Story: intro montage, opening cutscene, then the blizzard ride under keyboard control (W moves the horse). Zero faults in two runs of 15 and 12 minutes. Re-checked on 2026-10-05 on an M4 with the Wine 11 engine r15: launcher passed and the main menu reached at 200 s. Rockstar launcher error 113 on an environment moved off the Wine 10 engine came from leftover HKCU\Software\Wow6432Node registry keys, which hide Steam from the launcher's 32-bit lookup. A player found it, and Highball 0.10.16 links Steam's key back by itself. A player on an M5 plays it for almost two hours on the Wine 11 engine r23 with DXVK, with grass, bushes and trees flickering and changing as they move. On an external ultrawide display the game offered only three resolutions, all smaller than the screen, and fullscreen spilled past its edges (highball-db#272). Turning Tree Tessellation off does not stop the grass and tree flicker on an M5 (the reporter of highball-db#469 already had it off). A player reports a DirectX 12 route through D3DMetal instead (kevinzaracho, highball-db#579, 2026-10-20): 244 minutes on an Apple M3 with 16 GB, 1920x1080, Ultra textures, the tree pop-in gone, on engine x64-crossover26.3-r27 with the environment on D3DMetal. Their steps, from GameToMac's RDR2 profile: <API>kSettingAPI_DX12</API> in Documents/Rockstar Games/Red Dead Redemption 2/Settings/system.xml (the graphics mode alone leaves the game on Vulkan); D3DM_VENDOR_ID=0x106b and D3DM_DEVICE_DESCRIPTION=Apple Silicon (D3DMetal) in the environment's variables; under AppDefaults\RDR2.exe\DllOverrides atidxx64, d3d11, d3d12 and dxgi builtin, and nvapi64, nvngx and gameoverlayrenderer64 disabled; the Rockstar launcher kept on DXMT by copies of DXMT's d3d11, dxgi and d3d10core with the builtin marker removed, in system32 and the Launcher and Social Club folders, loaded native,builtin by Launcher.exe, LauncherPatcher.exe and SocialClubHelper.exe (in D3DMetal mode the launcher aborts on D3D11CoreCreateDevice and its browser stops on setDisplaySyncEnabled); and Steam's GPUAccelWebViewsV3 at 0, without which steamwebhelper hangs under D3DMetal. The first launch after the changes crashed the launcher after sign-in and the next one played. Which of these matter was not tested, and an engine change or a Windows setup rerun can put the original system32 files back. Not verified here.

games.notes: RE Engine, Direct3D 12 only, so D3DMetal. Two things happen on a first launch. First, Capcom's own first-run notice, a small 'CAPCOM InstallerMessage' window saying a 'VIDEO CODEC: WMVideo Decoder' must be installed: it is an unconditional notice, not a check (the program has no codec or registry test in it), so tick 'I accept the above message' and press Exit, and Steam starts the game. Second, the game then sits on a black screen with the process alive at under one percent CPU: its intro is a WMV video played through Wine's Windows Media reader, and on this engine that reader deadlocks. Measured with GStreamer's own debug log: the ASF demuxer fills one stream's queue to its 8 MB cap ('Queue is filled, signalling overrun') while the other stream never gets past preroll, and the demuxer blocks pushing to the full queue for as long as you wait. No renderer setting changes it (D3DMetal with MetalFX off measured the same). The Wine 11 engine was not exercised for this game here (the scripted Steam relaunch handshake got in the way), but it would not matter: the intro hang is in Wine's media reader, not the renderer or the Wine version. No fix yet; this is engine work in Wine's winegstreamer reader, and it affects the other RE Engine titles that play WMV intros the same way.

knownIssues.cause: macOS gives a legacy OpenGL context only at version 2.1, and the game asks for a legacy context then requires 3.0
knownIssues.fix: none in Highball
knownIssues.symptom: Exits at startup; the game's data/log.txt says 'needs OpenGL VBO support', with GLAD_GL_VERSION_3_0 0 in a 2.1 context

games.notes: Does not run. The game (GLFW and GLAD) asks for a legacy OpenGL context, gets the 2.1 context macOS allows for those, and then quits because it needs OpenGL 3.0 features (vertex buffer objects, 'needs OpenGL VBO support'). Apple only offers OpenGL above 2.1 as a core profile, which a program has to ask for, and the game asks for the old kind. Nothing in Highball's engines or recipes changes that: the CX_FWD_COMPAT_GL_CTX setting only helps programs that ask for 3.2 or newer. A software OpenGL (Mesa's llvmpipe) inside the environment is the only known way around it for games like this, not something Highball ships.
games.provenance: Reported by m0vi0 (highball-db#499, 2026-10-15), Apple M5, macOS 26.6.2, Highball 0.10.15, the default engine r26 and the Wine 11 engine r23, D3DMetal and DXMT modes: the game exits about ten seconds after starting on every one of them. Not verified by the maintainer.

knownIssues.cause: Reproduced on an Apple M1 Pro (2026-09-08, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2, DXMT). On the built-in display at 60 Hz the Metal HUD's frame interval sits steady near 9 ms while standing and spikes to about 21 ms with a jagged graph the moment the view turns; at 120 Hz on the same machine, same map, same mouse sweep, it stays flat near 6.7 ms with no spikes. So it is tied to the 60 Hz refresh rate and the frame presentation path at that rate, not the renderer (seen on DXMT) or the mouse input alone. The game's own vertical sync is a separate thing (it only capped the rate). Portal 2 on the same 60 Hz display is smooth, so it is specific to this game's rendering under Wine at 60 Hz.
knownIssues.fix: Reported and reproduced to be smooth at 120 Hz: play on a 120 Hz or ProMotion display, raw input on. On a 60 Hz display the camera jitter is open; capping the rate did not remove it.
knownIssues.symptom: On an external 60 Hz monitor the view jitters while the mouse moves (walking is smooth, only camera movement stutters), with raw input on, on DXMT and DXVK alike; the built-in ProMotion display with a 120 fps limit plays perfectly (M5 Pro).

games.notes: Plays. Reported on an M5 Pro over several sessions: on the built-in ProMotion display with Highball's frame rate limit at 120, DXMT, raw input on, it plays perfectly. On an external 60 Hz monitor the game's own "Wait for vertical sync" held the frame rate at 59.95; turning it off frees the frame rate, but the view still stutters while the mouse moves (smooth when walking, jitter only from camera movement), on DXMT uncapped and on DXVK alike; DXVK with Highball's limit at 60 and the game's at 120 is mainly playable with noticeable camera jitter. Kayf-Life shows the same; Portal 2 on the same monitor does not. A second reporter played 185 minutes on DXVK on an M3 Max with macOS 27 and rated it playable with minor issues. The same reporter later rated it perfect on DXVK with Highball's limit at 60 on engine r11, after 100 minutes. Not tried here. A later report has it perfect on DXVK with Highball's frame rate limit at 60 on an M4 with macOS 26.6.2, engine r7, after 10 minutes. Checked here on 2026-10-05 on an M4 with engine r21 (DEP kept on), the 64-bit build: the main menu comes up at 130 s with Find a Game ready; no match played.

knownIssues.cause: measured: the video needs a Direct3D 11 shared texture; Wine 10 fails in the decoder, Wine 11 before r11 got no handle from DXMT, and DXVK cannot share textures at all
knownIssues.fix: Engine r11 or later with DXMT (patch 0010). On DXVK the menu keeps a still image; the game plays anyway.

games.notes: Needs the Wine 11 engine x64-crossover26.3-r11 or later (the recipe names it). Two bugs sat behind the report, both in Wine on macOS and both fixed in r11. Start did nothing because the game's save code asks Windows for the last error after a file call and, on macOS, the place Unity's Mono reads it from (%gs:0x68) held a stray pointer instead of the error code, so a missing save file became an IOException that ended the click (Player.log: IOException: Unknown error (0x...)). The menu's 2560x1440 H.264 video, played through Media Foundation and handed to Direct3D 11 as a shared texture, got no shared handle from DXMT on Wine 11 (Got null handle from IDXGIResource::GetSharedHandle) and failed inside the decoder on Wine 10. On r11 both are gone: the run starts on DXMT and on DXVK, and the video plays on DXMT. DXVK draws the board at 20 fps against DXMT's 86 and shows a still behind the menu instead of the video, so use DXMT. On the default Wine 10 engine neither fix exists, but the error path needs the save file to be missing, which is what a first run looks like: with a save already there the game plays on Wine 10 too, measured here on 2026-09-22 (M1 Pro, macOS 27.0, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r5, DXMT, a full session with runs started and no exception in Player.log, the save having arrived through Steam Cloud). So the Wine 11 engine is what a new player needs, and someone whose save already exists may never see the fault.

verified.fps: 128 in live mode on a lot, 130 on the world map (DXMT fork 7421db2, Metal HUD)

knownIssues.cause: reported by two people, both on an M4 (M4 with macOS 27 and DXVK, M4 Pro with macOS 26.5.2 and DXMT), so it is not tied to one graphics mode. Not reproduced here on an M1 Pro, where the neighbourhood and an empty lot drew correctly at the default resolution on 2026-09-21; the two reporters describe it differently, one saying it shows at a high in-game resolution (2880x1620) once a house is built, the other that it shows from the start and survives a restart of the game. The pattern, small textures arriving as uninitialised memory, points at the host-memory import path this 32-bit Vulkan game needs (MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT=1). Checked on an M4 here on 2026-10-03 (macOS 27.0, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r19, the recipe's MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT=1 confirmed in the process): the neighbourhood map, the Goth lot with its walls, floors and pool, and Buy mode all drew correctly, with no MoltenVK error over ten minutes. The sims themselves and a lot's family portrait were not reached in that scripted run, so the reported part is still neither reproduced nor ruled out on an M4.
knownIssues.fix: None yet. The game plays through it; tracked from highball-db#160.
knownIssues.symptom: Sims drawn as black silhouettes on the lot, and in the neighbourhood view the family portrait is coloured noise and the lot preview a black block

games.notes: Re-verified on engine r2 on 2026-09-10: launches from Steam and reaches the neighbourhood view at 99.3 fps, 1728x1117, 2.8 ms of GPU per frame, presenting directly rather than through the compositor. No MoltenVK device losses in the run, so the shadow-import fix is holding. EA's 2025 re-release draws with Vulkan rather than Direct3D, so the renderer setting has no effect on it; the bottle's renderer is irrelevant (dxvk here). It needs engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r1 or newer plus the Sims recipe, which sets MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT=1. On older engines the window opens black with the game running behind it: the game is 32-bit, Wine imports its own host memory into MoltenVK, and Metal loses the device on the first frame (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory, six times, then nothing). With the patched engine it plays: neighbourhood and lot load, Sims take orders, 65 fps at 1728x1117. Reported black-screen elsewhere on M4 and M5 machines (highball-db issue #7, KhronosGroup/MoltenVK#2766); the fix is not chip-specific. Run again on an M4 on 2026-10-03 (macOS 27.0, engine r19): with the recipe's variable in the process the neighbourhood and a lot draw correctly; without it the window is black and MoltenVK loses the device at the first frame, as the older-engine note above says. Re-checked on 2026-10-05 on an M4 with engine r21 (DEP kept on): the neighbourhood view draws as before. Live mode checked on 2026-10-06 on an M4 (macOS 27.0, r21, MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT=1): the tutorial family's lot with a Sim on screen, zoomed in with the clock running, once at 1440x1080 and once with Retina resolution on (a 3840x2160 screen for the game). The Sim drew correctly both times, no black figures or noise, no lost device in the log. The black Sims and missing portraits reported on M4s with engine r5 (highball-db#160, #174) did not reproduce; family portraits were not brought on screen.

Apply the warframe recipe first: it turns DirectWrite off for the game's launcher only (Tools\Launcher.exe), whose embedded browser otherwise paints a black window on this engine, the same DirectWrite problem as Sikarugir #255. With that override the launcher shows its EULA, updates the game and starts it. The game itself needs nothing. Use DXMT: the first tutorial mission, with combat, ran at about 35 fps at 1728x1117 borderless (the game's own low preset, 1280x720 render, anti-aliasing and ambient occlusion off) with the Metal HUD reading 28 ms of GPU per frame; later in the same session, past the tutorial, the maintainer's own play ran above 100 fps by the HUD. DXVK also reaches the mission but is GPU-bound at about 16 fps (51 ms GPU) with the same settings. 'Login with Steam' works; a Steam account without a Warframe account gets the game's own bind-or-create dialog, which is normal. A sleeping display stalls the game for as long as it sleeps, so keep the Mac awake for long sessions. Verified 2026-09-04 on macOS 26.6.2, M1 Pro: launcher update, Steam login, account creation, tutorial mission and later play; Exit Game shuts the process down cleanly (the game log ends with its normal shutdown). A D3DMetal report on the 0.10.4 beta on an M3 Pro with macOS 27 rates it perfect across every planet and environment with HDR on, with a frame rate drop in Duviri that the reporter says every platform shows. Which engine ran it is not settled, the id in the report matches none, and on macOS 27 D3DMetal is 3.0 on the default r19 or 4.0 beta 2 on the opt-in r20. No frame rate was given for that session. Letting the bundled dgVoodoo load (DLL overrides ddraw,d3dimm,d3drm=n,b) gets a Direct3D 11 device and a 640x480 exclusive swapchain through DXMT or DXVK, then dgVoodoo's ddraw crashes with a page fault right after DXGI sets a 960x600 at 120 Hz display mode, with dgVoodoo set to Direct3D 11 feature level 10.0 or 11.0, windowed or not, with or without EmulateModeset. Tried here on an M4 with macOS 27.0 on 2026-10-05, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r21, the Steam copy: the game asks Windows for 640x480 at 16 bits, Wine on the Mac offers only the display's own mode, and the game stops with 'incompatible DirectX version or out-of-date display drivers'. Wine's emulated display modes set for DarkOmen.exe alone do not help, because Wine builds its list of modes in another process; set for the whole environment they do, the error goes away and a 4:3 picture area opens, but it stayed black for 200 s without input. steps.text: Before first launch, install .NET Framework 4.8 from the bottle's Dependencies section (20 to 40 minutes; looks frozen for long stretches, let it finish). AC's launcher is a 32-bit .NET/WPF app and dies silently without it — this was the historical 'AC won't launch' failure.
Use D3DMetal. Under DXMT the session loads and the engine runs (physics ticks, log fills) but nothing ever paints — black screen after clicking start. Verified on this engine 2026-08-28.
The launcher's news panels can spin forever (embedded Chromium fetching old feeds). Cosmetic — Drive, Career and settings all work.

Custom Shaders Patch, if you install it through Content Manager, hooks the game through a dwrite.dll it drops next to acs.exe. Wine prefers its own dwrite unless told otherwise, so this setup lets the game's copy load first, for acs.exe only (nothing changes for a game without CSP, Wine's own dwrite is used as before). CSP then wants Windows fonts its config names, Segoe UI, Consolas and Orbitron among them, which an environment does not have and Highball cannot ship. Put them in the environment's C:\windows\Fonts folder (a Windows install or the community font pack has them). Without them the session crashes at start with CSP on. Measured by a player on an M1 Pro with Highball 0.10.4 (highball#243).

The game's videos (the opening one and the one after the difficulty selection) freeze it a few seconds in: Wine's media pipeline deadlocks on them, on every graphics mode. With Media Foundation's platform library disabled for BloodySpell.exe only, the game no longer hangs, the intro still plays, and it goes in game (confirmed by the reporter of highball-db#316 with the same override set by hand). Microsoft's core fonts come along because the title screen's text does not render without them. Nothing else in the environment changes.

lastVerified.result: Full game (Steam 2698780) on the Wine 11 engines. On r11, DXVK: intros, a loading screen with a progress bar, then the character creator after about five minutes, its hair and beard tabs clicked through by the owner, character preview black. On r11, DXMT: the character creator with the 3D scene and the character drawn, no crash. On r12, DXMT: the same process profile over four minutes (memory climbing to 1 GB then settling, three cores busy, no crash, no crash report), the screen itself not captured because the Mac's session was locked. On the Wine 10 engine r7 the same install never leaves its loading screen. Gameplay past the character creator not exercised, frame rate not read.

steps.text: ContractVille runs on the Wine 11 engine and not on the Wine 10 one. On the default engine the game sits on its loading screen forever after the logos, with the game running and nothing loading (highball#202, reproduced on an M1 Pro). On the Wine 11 tree the same install loads, plays its intros and reaches the character creator. DXMT is the mode to use there: DXVK on Wine 11 gets through but draws the character preview black, and DXMT on the Wine 10 engine crashes at start on a shared texture. So this fix only names the engine and the mode, nothing in the environment changes.

steps.text: CS2 itself needs no setup: Highball picks the graphics mode from the game's row (DXMT on macOS 15 and newer, DXVK below). This recipe's settings are for the legacy CS:GO branch (32-bit, D3D9, csgo.exe): async shader compile off (map-load freeze, issue #21), a 2 GB texture-memory report for the 32-bit process, and a real Radeon device id so Source picks the ATI shadow path.

knownIssues.cause: MoltenVK loses the device on Source's zero-attachment HDR pass (highball#34), and a second stall after the console reaches INGAME that is not yet explained.
knownIssues.fix: This recipe: wined3d plus the NVIDIA identity for csgo.exe on engine r7.
knownIssues.symptom: On the default (DXVK) graphics mode on macOS 26: the map load stops at 'Initializing game data' or the screen goes black at the end of the load.

lastVerified.result: Dust II with bots plays at 17 fps (1728x1117, defaults) on an M1 Pro: main menu, map load, spawn, a round with movement and damage. Verified through this recipe on a fresh r7 install with the environment on DXMT, so the Steam client draws as usual.

steps.text: Needs engine x64-crossover26.3-r7 or later. The game gets the engine's own Direct3D 9 (wined3d, on OpenGL) as a d3d9.dll in its bin folder, loaded first for csgo.exe only, so this one game runs on wined3d while the environment and the Steam client keep their graphics mode. On DXVK's Direct3D 9 the map load on macOS 26 either loses the GPU device on Source's HDR pass or never finishes.

The two registry values give csgo.exe alone an NVIDIA identity (GeForce GTX 1080, 0x10de:0x1b80). Source's shadow-map check passes on NVIDIA's depth-texture path, which wined3d supports, and fails on AMD's, which it does not. With an NVIDIA identity the game insists on NVIDIA's driver library, which r7's engine answers with a stub. Other programs in the bottle keep Highball's AMD identity.

Legacy CS:GO is Valve's free standalone app 4465480; Highball launches it directly. The Metal HUD does not show on this game because OpenGL presents the frames, so use the game's own cl_showfps or net_graph for a frame rate.

lastVerified.result: DXVK: with the setting, the game fills a 1728x1117 display edge to edge and centred, confirmed by eye twice (bottle-wide value, then this per-application value). steps.text: The game asks Windows for a 1280x800 fullscreen mode. Wine's Mac driver cannot switch a Mac display for it, and without this setting it reported success while leaving the display as it was, so the picture landed down and to the right with black bars and a clipped edge on any display that is not 16:10. With EmulateModeset, Wine emulates the mode change itself (the game sees its 1280x800, Wine scales the fullscreen window to the real screen), and the picture fills the screen and centres. Scoped to the game's executable; nothing else in the environment changes.

steps.text: Forza Horizon 6 needs macOS 27 and the Wine 11 engine r18, which carries Apple's D3DMetal 4. Its copy protection opens files in a way the Wine 10 engine does not handle, and it refuses D3DMetal 3 as an unsupported graphics card (FH205). D3DMetal presents itself as an AMD card by default, and the game then crashes in its AMD-only code (its FHE21 dialog), so this recipe has D3DMetal report an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 instead. The game then offers NVIDIA Reflex, and DLSS Super Resolution when Enable DLSS (MetalFX) is on in the environment's Graphics settings (Highball 0.10.23 or later): D3DMetal runs it on MetalFX. DLSS Frame Generation stays unavailable. The first start spends about three minutes at 'Optimizing for your PC'. The game asks you to sign in to Xbox once with a code at microsoft.com/link, and remembers it from then on. On a base M4 at 1080p expect about 28 fps on the High preset the game picks, 38 on Medium with FSR Balanced (Video settings), 50 on Very Low.

knownIssues.cause: the sign-in is a browser surface drawn by a separate GPU process into the launcher's window, which Wine returned nothing for until engine patch 0007.
knownIssues.fix: use engine x64-crossover26.3-r5 or later with the DXMT renderer. The rockstar recipe sets DXMT_ALLOW_CROSS_PROCESS_SWAPCHAIN=1, which is also required.
knownIssues.symptom: The Rockstar launcher shows a blank sign-in window and the game never starts.

lastVerified.result: dxmt: story mode reached and played, 60-120 fps at 1280x800 windowed with VSync off. The Rockstar launcher renders and signs in. Online untested and impossible (BattlEye).

steps.text: Asks for the Wine 11 engine r15 or newer since 2026-10-03 (was r5). On r11 to r14 the Rockstar Games Launcher installer stops at once, and an environment already on an older revision is not moved on its own, so raising the pin makes Play offer the newest revision to those environments. Everything installed stays.
Needs engine x64-crossover26.3-r5 or later. Earlier engines cannot render the Rockstar launcher's sign-in window, which is a browser view drawn by a separate process, so the game can never start.
Story mode only. GTA Online uses BattlEye, a kernel-level anti-cheat, which cannot run under Wine on any tool.

If sign-in fails with 'we are unable to handle your request at this time', check the Mac's clock: System Settings, General, Date & Time, with the time zone set automatically. A wrong clock is refused by Rockstar and looks like an account or network problem.

knownIssues.cause: this build has no dxsupport.cfg (none in bin or in any VPK), and its first-start autodetect picks DirectX level 80 on a Mac under wined3d, DXVK and DXMT alike, whatever GPU identity it sees (measured on an M4, 2026-10-07)
knownIssues.fix: this optional recipe. A stored DXLevel_V1 sticks only next to the DeviceID and VendorID of the card the game sees, which is why the recipe writes Wine's own Direct3D identity (0x1002, 0x73BF) with it. A lone DXLevel_V1 is re-detected to 80

lastVerified.result: With these four values Half-Life 2 starts at DirectX level 95 under Wine's own Direct3D (mat_dxlevel 95, mat_hdr_level 2), and d1_trainstation_01 loads and draws with HDR lighting, no device loss. Without them a fresh start picks 80 under wined3d, DXVK and DXMT. The game's bench.dem timedemo at 1280x720 windowed: 65.5 and 64.6 fps at level 80, 52.2 and 51.6 fps at level 95.

steps.text: Optional. This build of Half-Life 2 ships no table of graphics cards, so on its first start on a Mac it picks its DirectX 8 path whatever the graphics mode: no HDR lighting, simpler water and shaders. This fix stores the DirectX 9 level (95) with the graphics card Wine's own Direct3D presents, so the game keeps it. It costs about a fifth of the frame rate: 65 fps against 52 in the game's own benchmark on an M4. It works with Wine's own Direct3D, the mode this game's page picks. In another mode the game goes back to its DirectX 8 path by itself.

steps.text: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 runs on Highball's native arm64 preview engine, which this recipe asks for, and the Intel engines cannot start it. The engine needs macOS 26.5 or later. It was tested on a Mac with 32 GB of memory, where the game used 25 to 27 GB. The first start takes about seven minutes to the start screen and four more from Start to the cockpit, and later starts reuse the shader and code caches. On a base M4 in daylight, expect 22 to 25 fps parked and 19 to 21 on the take-off roll at the Medium preset with FSR Balanced. Turn Motion Blur off in the graphics settings.

The Steam copy runs through the EA app, which Steam installs on the game's first start and which only installs on the Wine 11 engine (highball-db#318). This recipe asks for that engine and installs the EA app first; sign in to it once, then start the game from Steam. The game itself has not been verified here yet.
Without this file the game can sit on its loading screen after the main menu for good; with it the game's Steam support initialises on its own and the load finishes (a player's fix, highball#322).

Capcom's RE Engine asks DirectX 12 for 64-bit atomics on descriptor heap resources and refuses the graphics card without them. On M1 and M2 chips Apple's D3DMetal answers no, so this recipe moves the game to the Wine 11 engine r25 or later, whose DirectX 12 layer in front of D3DMetal answers yes when HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 is set, and sets it. Confirmed by a player on an M1 Pro with the unmodified D3DMetal 3 (Highball 0.10.16). On an M4 D3DMetal answers yes by itself and the variable changes nothing.

steps.text: Paperback runs on the Wine 11 engine r21 and on no engine before it. The game (Loom engine, SDL and OpenGL) loads glClearDepthf in the OpenGL 2.1 context macOS gives it, where older engines hand it nothing, so it crashed at address 0 a second after start on every engine and graphics mode (highball-db#349). r21 answers that call and four like it in old-style contexts (engine patch 0021), and both of the game's builds reach the title menu there. The graphics mode does not apply to an OpenGL game, so this fix only names the engine, nothing in the environment changes.
