knownIssues.fix: the recipe asks for engine x64-crossover26.3-r8
knownIssues.symptom: Does not run on the Sikarugir (Wine 10) engines

steps.text: Reported playing on the CrossOver-tree engine (highball-db#22, M5, macOS 27.0): D3DMetal rated 5 of 5 on r7, DXMT running on r8 at 26 fps in Shibuya at 1280x800 on a throttling Mac. The reporter says the Sikarugir (Wine 10) engines do not run it and that r8 loads more stably than r7, so the recipe asks for r8. Highball asks for Apple's licence the first time D3DMetal is used.

On engine r7, DXMT with the cross-process swapchain switch kernel-panicked the reporter's Mac. On r8 the reporter says DXMT works and the panic did not recur. Not measured by the maintainer, so the recipe keeps D3DMetal, the rated mode; switch the game to DXMT in Advanced if you want to try it on r8.

knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed; the Cellar profile this recipe carries was reported working on an M5. A first run in the same session went to a Steam client started before the variables were set, which reproduced the original crash dialog once.
knownIssues.fix: none confirmed on an M3 Pro. Do not force-stop the environment while the game is up under D3DMetal, quit from the game if it ever shows; close Steam and Play again after changing the environment's variables so the client carries them
knownIssues.symptom: With the recipe's configuration in place (Wine 11 r9, D3DMetal, Metal's validation layer on, confirmed by 'Metal API Validation Enabled' in the launch log) the game shows nothing for five minutes; stopping the environment then froze the whole Mac and needed a forced reboot (highball-db#115, Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, 2026-09-18)

knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed; same shape as the M3 Pro report above
knownIssues.fix: none known
knownIssues.symptom: On an M5 Pro (macOS 27.0.1, engine r18 with D3DMetal 4 and r19 with D3DMetal 3) the game process stays alive with no window, and the Mac becomes unresponsive within minutes and needs a restart (highball-db#356, 2026-10-06)

knownIssues.cause: two things stack: DXMT has no Direct3D 12 at all, and on the Wine 10 engines D3DMetal hits a startup race that ends the game within seconds. Cellar's profile documents the race and the Wine 10.8+ requirement.
knownIssues.fix: Apply this recipe on the Wine 11 engine it asks for. The Cellar workaround (MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 and MTL_DEBUG_LAYER_ERROR_MODE=nslog) is not recommended: on an M3 Pro and an M5 Pro it led to a frozen Mac that needed a restart
knownIssues.symptom: Crash dialog offering to send diagnostics to the developer right at launch (reported highball-db#115, DXMT and D3DMetal, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2 and r3)

steps.text: Direct3D 12 only, so D3DMetal, and it needs a Wine 11 engine (Wine 10.8 or newer): on the Wine 10 engines it dies at start with the game's own crash dialog even on D3DMetal. Highball offers the engine before applying this. Denuvo, so Steam must be signed in. Not yet run here. Until 2026-10-06 this recipe also turned on Metal's validation layer (MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 with MTL_DEBUG_LAYER_ERROR_MODE=nslog), the Cellar project's workaround for a D3DMetal startup race, reported playable on an M5 there. With it, two Macs here (an M3 Pro and an M5 Pro) froze and needed a restart, so it was removed. Without it, the expected failure is the game's crash dialog at start, which is the safer one.

knownIssues.cause: Source's HDR auto-exposure pass draws occlusion queries into a render pass with no attachments, which the Apple GPU can fail on inside MoltenVK, the same freeze Portal 2 had. Seen on an M1 Pro with engine r0 (2026-08-28). On an M4 with engine r21 Portal's HDR loaded even without the switch below (2026-10-07).
knownIssues.fix: mat_tonemapping_occlusion_use_stencil 1 (this recipe writes it into portal/cfg/autoexec.cfg) runs that pass on the stencil buffer. Checked on an M4, macOS 27.0, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r21, DXVK, 2026-10-07: testchmb_a_00 and testchmb_a_08 load with HDR on and the first portals draw. Turning HDR off (mat_hdr_level 0) still works as a fallback.
knownIssues.symptom: Freeze or crash at the end of map loads with HDR enabled

lastVerified.result: HDR on with mat_tonemapping_occlusion_use_stencil 1: testchmb_a_00 loads and plays its opening (the countdown runs, the scripted orange and blue portals open with the Relaxation Vault drawn through them), testchmb_a_08 loads, no device loss. HDR on without the switch also loaded testchmb_a_00 here. DirectX level 95 after a fresh autodetect (this build ships dxsupport.cfg). Earlier, with HDR off on an M1 Pro, macOS 14.6, engine r0: about 96 fps in the first chamber (2026-08-28).

steps.text: Portal runs with HDR on, with the lighting and bloom it has on Windows. On a Mac, Source's HDR auto-exposure pass used to make map loads freeze or crash, so this recipe turned HDR off. It now sets mat_tonemapping_occlusion_use_stencil 1, Source's own switch that runs that pass on the stencil buffer, the fix that brought HDR back in Portal 2. If loads ever freeze, turn HDR off again by changing mat_hdr_level 2 to 0 in portal/cfg/autoexec.cfg. Keep the game on DXVK.

knownIssues.cause: Source's HDR auto-exposure pass draws occlusion queries into a render pass with no attachments, and the Apple GPU loses the device on it inside MoltenVK (VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, Metal 'Internal Error (0000010d)', and Metal API and shader validation report nothing before it). Engine-level, and it affects other Source titles too.
knownIssues.fix: mat_tonemapping_occlusion_use_stencil 1 (this recipe writes it into portal2/cfg/autoexec.cfg) runs that pass on the stencil buffer, so it has an attachment, and HDR works. Measured on an M4 with macOS 27.0, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r21 and DXVK on 2026-10-07, in nine map loads with HDR on across sp_a1_intro1, sp_a1_intro2, sp_a1_intro3 and sp_a2_laser_intro, the last two with this recipe applied by Highball itself. No device loss, and portals drawn correctly. Without the switch every HDR load lost the device. Earlier this recipe turned HDR off (mat_hdr_level 0), which still works as a fallback.
knownIssues.symptom: Freeze or crash at the end of every map load (white or stuck screen), menus fine

knownIssues.cause: Portal 2's shaderapidx9 sizes video memory through WMI (Win32_VideoController). Wine answers AdapterRAM 4294967295 (0xFFFFFFFF) under DXVK, the game reads it as -1 (mat_info: m_TextureMemorySize -1, Size of Texture Memory 0 kb) and its autodetect saves gpu_mem_level 0. Seen on an M1 Pro (16 GB) and an M4 (32 GB), 2026-10-06.
knownIssues.fix: this recipe sets HKCU\Software\Wine\AppDefaults\portal2.exe\Direct3D VideoMemorySize = 2047, then the game reports 2047 MB and saves gpu_mem_level 2 (High). Verified on the M4, macOS 27.0, r21. A config saved before needs Model / Texture Detail set to High once by hand.
knownIssues.symptom: Textures look softer than on Windows. Options, Video, Advanced shows Model / Texture Detail on Low after the first start

lastVerified.result: HDR on with mat_tonemapping_occlusion_use_stencil 1 in nine map loads (sp_a1_intro3 four times, sp_a1_intro1 and sp_a1_intro2 twice each, sp_a2_laser_intro once), the last two with this recipe applied by highball recipe apply. No device loss, HDR lighting, bloom and fog drawn, and an orange and a blue portal opened from the console drawn with the far side visible. Without the switch, every HDR load lost the device (four runs on sp_a1_intro1 and sp_a1_intro3). Earlier verifications with HDR off on an M1 Pro, macOS 14.6 and 26.6.2 (2026-08-28, 2026-09-02).

steps.text: Portal 2 runs with HDR on, with the lighting, bloom and haze it has on Windows. On a Mac, Source's HDR auto-exposure pass used to make every map load freeze or crash, because it draws into a pass with nothing attached, which the Mac's GPU driver gives up on. This recipe sets mat_tonemapping_occlusion_use_stencil 1, Source's own switch that runs that pass on the stencil buffer instead, and HDR then loads and plays. If loads ever freeze with a white or stuck screen, turn HDR off again by changing mat_hdr_level 2 to 0 in portal2/cfg/autoexec.cfg and in portal2/cfg/video.txt. Keep the game on DXVK.

Portal 2 sizes video memory from Windows' WMI, where Wine reports 4294967295 bytes on a Mac with a lot of memory. The game reads that as -1 and picks its lowest Model / Texture Detail on its first start. The recipe tells Wine to report 2047 MB to portal2.exe, so the game picks High. A config saved before this keeps its old setting: set Model / Texture Detail to High in Options, Video, Advanced once.

Capcom's RE Engine asks DirectX 12 for 64-bit atomics on descriptor heap resources and refuses the graphics card without them. On M1 and M2 chips Apple's D3DMetal answers no, so this recipe moves the game to the Wine 11 engine r25 or later, whose DirectX 12 layer in front of D3DMetal answers yes when HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 is set, and sets it. Confirmed by a player on an M1 Pro with the unmodified D3DMetal 3 (Highball 0.10.16). On an M4 D3DMetal answers yes by itself and the variable changes nothing.

knownIssues.cause: reported: the DXVK-Kegworks 1.10.4 Direct3D 9 loses the Metal device on this game
knownIssues.fix: apply this optional fix under Advanced on the game's page; if the picture turns grayscale, remove the copied d3d9.dll next to RRRE64.exe and the override, both reported outcomes exist
knownIssues.symptom: Pre-race screen freezes after the track loads, VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST in the Direct3D 9 log (default layer)

knownIssues.cause: measured 2026-09-20 on Half-Life 2 with +loaddll: on a DXVK launch the engine's own Direct3D 9 overlay is found before the copy beside the game's executable (the launch's WINEDLLOVERRIDES outranks the per-program registry entry), so the newer layer never loads; it loads on a wined3d launch
knownIssues.fix: none shipped yet; a per-program layer choice is planned (Highball plan item 14). Setting this game's mode to Wine's own Direct3D makes the copy the Direct3D 9 in use, untested on RaceRoom
knownIssues.symptom: Applying this fix changes nothing on a DXVK launch

steps.text: Optional, never applied by Play: puts the DXVK-MacOS 3.1 Direct3D 9 (the engine's d9vk-modern directory) beside RRRE64.exe with a per-program override, so this game alone runs on it while every other game keeps the default layer. It rendered the game, practice and races with AI, for one reporter on an M3 whose sessions froze with VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST on the default layer (highball-db#60); when the withdrawn r4 engine put the same layer on every launch's path, another reporter got RaceRoom in grayscale and a third had Five Nights at Freddy's freeze, so it is offered under Advanced rather than applied. On the maintainer's M1 Pro the same DLL runs Five Nights at Freddy's without a freeze (2026-09-18). RaceRoom itself is not installed here (74 GB).

knownIssues.cause: MoltenVK 1.4.1 refuses linear-tiled 3D, mipmapped and array images (fixed in r6's MoltenVK). D3DMetal answers a D3D12 call the game needs with 'Not implemented' (not fixable here).
knownIssues.fix: use engine x64-crossover26.3-r6 or later and leave the game on its default Vulkan renderer.
knownIssues.symptom: On engines before r6: loads to about 98 per cent, opens a window and exits without a frame (Vulkan), or crashes about 30 seconds in with DirectX 12 selected in system.xml.

knownIssues.cause: SPIRV-Cross's Metal output for cull distance, and the row pitch of the game's linear 2D textures.
knownIssues.fix: none needed so far: nothing visibly missing in the prologue. Recorded so a texture glitch later has a lead.
knownIssues.symptom: One vertex shader fails to compile to Metal (gl_CullDistance emitted into an undeclared struct member) and the driver logs many bytes_per_row assertions during loading.

knownIssues.cause: a Highball engine patch from r11 returned a heap pointer from GetLastError() after the first display call of a process; the installer reads it right after it measures the display.
knownIssues.fix: engine x64-crossover26.3-r15 (Highball 0.10.3). r7, the revision this recipe names, does not have the fault.
knownIssues.symptom: On engines r11 to r14 the Rockstar Games Launcher installer stops right after it starts with 'make sure all instances of the Rockstar Games Launcher have been closed' and the launcher is never installed.

lastVerified.result: Fresh environment, launcher installed through the Rockstar recipe, then Highball's Play: Steam cold-started into the game, the launcher mirrored the Steam entitlement and started RDR2.exe, which reached its brightness calibration screen. The 2026-09-11 run on an M1 Pro (r6, macOS 26.6.2) played the prologue.

steps.text: Asks for the Wine 11 engine r15 or newer since 2026-10-03 (was r7). On r11 to r14 the Rockstar Games Launcher installer stops at once, and an environment already on an older revision is not moved on its own, so raising the pin makes Play offer the newest revision to those environments. Everything installed stays.

Needs engine x64-crossover26.3-r6 or later (the recipe asks for r7, which carries the same MoltenVK plus the NVAPI stub other games need): its MoltenVK accepts the linear-tiled 3D, mipmapped and array images the game creates. On every earlier engine the game exits at 98 per cent of its first load.

Install the Rockstar Games Launcher through Highball first (Add games, Rockstar) rather than letting Steam's first run install it: on engines r11 to r14 Steam's installer stops at once with 'make sure all instances of the Rockstar Games Launcher have been closed' (fixed in r15), and on r7 the launcher installed through Highball initialised Steam and started the game on an M4 (2026-10-02).
Leave the game on its own Vulkan renderer (the default). The graphics mode setting applies to the Rockstar launcher, which needs DXMT, not to the game.

Tested at 1280x720 windowed, set in Documents/Rockstar Games/Red Dead Redemption 2/Settings/system.xml (<screenWidth>, <screenHeight>, <windowed value="1" />) after the first run writes the file. About 34 fps in the prologue snow on an M1 Pro.
The first key after the game window regains focus is ignored. Press it again.

On a 16 GB Mac the game is memory-bound: its footprint passes 13 GB in the prologue and macOS swaps, so the frame rate decays over a minute of play. In Documents/Rockstar Games/Red Dead Redemption 2/Settings/system.xml, vSync 0 and fsr2Index 2 (FSR 2 balanced) keep the menus and cutscenes smoother and halve the GPU time there; they do not remove the memory wall. 24 GB or more removes it.

Epic copy: Highball 0.9.12 or later starts it through a stand-in for Epic's launcher so the Rockstar launcher accepts the entitlement. If the game then stops with Error 18 (its Vulkan layer missing), copy vulkan-1.dll from Program Files/Rockstar Games/Social Club next to RDR2.exe in the game folder; the per-program override above makes the game use it. Reported on an M5 Max on engine r8, main menu reached at 1080p ultra (highball#93).

lastVerified.result: Demo (3916150) on D3DMetal: with the override, title screen and full main menu render, confirmed by eye on r5 and on r6 (GPTK 4 D3DMetal); without it, black window, Metal assertion in the log, main thread stuck. The exe name is the same in the demo and the full game.

steps.text: The menu plays a 4K 60 fps video (Content/Movies/Menubgvideo4k60.mp4) through Windows Media Foundation. Under Wine the decoded frames reach D3DMetal as a texture it has no Metal format for: Metal refuses the descriptor (invalid pixelFormat 0), the thread that asked dies, and the game's main thread then waits on it forever, so the window stays black at idle GPU. With Media Foundation's platform library disabled for the game's executable only, the media player fails to open the file, the menu comes up without its background video, and the game plays. Nothing else in the environment changes.

knownIssues.cause: Wine on macOS kept GetLastError in a different thread slot from the one MSVC-built Mono reads (highball-engine patch 0011)
knownIssues.fix: This recipe's engine, r11 or later. The fault needs the save to be missing, so it hits a first run; a copy that already has a save plays on Wine 10 too (measured 2026-09-22).
knownIssues.symptom: Pressing Start or Embark does nothing on a first run; Player.log has IOException: Unknown error (0x...) on the save file

knownIssues.cause: Its shared Direct3D 11 texture got no handle from DXMT before r11 (patch 0010); DXVK cannot share textures at all
knownIssues.fix: r11 or later with DXMT. On DXVK the game plays with a still behind the menu.
knownIssues.symptom: The menu's background video does not show

lastVerified.result: Free Prologue (Steam 2517810, the same Unity player as the full game) on DXMT, three launches: menu with its video, Embark, hero and relic picks, the Act I map, the first fight won at 76 fps, quit through the menu with the save written. One launch on DXVK continued a save to the board at 20 fps. Zero exceptions in Player.log.

steps.text: Needs engine x64-crossover26.3-r11 or later. Two Wine-on-macOS bugs are fixed there and nowhere else: the last-error slot Unity's Mono reads held a stray pointer, so a missing save file ended the Start click with IOException Unknown error, and the menu video's shared texture got no handle from DXMT. On the Wine 10 engines pressing Start still does nothing and no setting changes that.
Use DXMT. DXVK also starts the run on r11 but draws the board at 20 fps against DXMT's 86 on an M1 Pro, and its menu shows a still image where DXMT plays the video.

knownIssues.cause: 32-bit game with a native Vulkan renderer: Wine's wow64 layer imports its own host memory into MoltenVK for host-visible allocations, and Metal fails every vkQueueSubmit over those no-copy pages with kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory (verified 2026-09-02 on macOS 26.6.2, M1 Pro; same signature as KhronosGroup/MoltenVK#2766 on an M5).
knownIssues.fix: Engine r1 or newer plus MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT=1 (this recipe). Verified: with the patched MoltenVK and the flag, zero device losses and the game plays; with the same build and the flag off, six device losses and a black screen.
knownIssues.symptom: Black window on launch, game and audio running behind it

lastVerified.result: Through the shipped path (engine r1's patched MoltenVK 1.4.1, this recipe's MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT=1, cold Steam start, launched from Steam): neighbourhood view renders at 117 fps, 1728x1117 (Metal HUD), frames live for 90 s. Earlier the same day with the experimental 1.4.2 build: lot loads, a Sim takes orders, 65 fps, clean exit. Same build with the flag off: six lost devices and a black screen.

steps.text: This game draws with Vulkan, not Direct3D, so the renderer setting does nothing for it. What it needs is engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r1 or newer, whose MoltenVK carries Highball's shadow-import patch, plus the MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT=1 this recipe sets. Without both, the window opens black: the game's Vulkan device is lost on its first frame and never recovers.

knownIssues.cause: measured by the reporter with WINEDEBUG=+wgl: the game requests an OpenGL 3.2 core context without the forward-compatible bit and Wine's Mac driver refuses it
knownIssues.fix: this recipe sets CX_FWD_COMPAT_GL_CTX=1, confirmed by the reporter
knownIssues.symptom: Crashes right after launch on every graphics mode, page fault at address zero (reported on an M1 Pro, macOS 27)

knownIssues.cause: Wine's Mac driver renders at the logical resolution unless RetinaMode is on
knownIssues.fix: set the environment's display scaling to 200 percent (Wine's Retina mode), reported by the same person
knownIssues.symptom: Pixelated picture, the game renders at 1512x982 and is upscaled (reported on an M1 Pro)

steps.text: An OpenGL game. It asks Wine's Mac driver for a 3.2 core context without the forward-compatible bit, which macOS requires, so the driver returned nothing and the game crashed on its first OpenGL call, on every graphics mode. The CrossOver switch the engine's Mac driver carries adds the bit (found and confirmed by the reporter of highball#136 on an M1 Pro, macOS 27). For a sharp picture set the environment's display scaling to 200 percent, which turns on Wine's Retina mode; the reporter saw an upscaled 1512x982 without it.

Japanese fonts are installed by the fakejapanese recipe this one pulls in, so Japanese names and chat draw instead of blank squares. One report so far (highball-db#206): playable on DXVK on the Wine 11 engine r8 with the reporter's own fonts. The default Wine 10 engine and the recipe's fonts are not yet confirmed on this game.

Vaultbreakers is DirectX 12 only and stops with its own 'DirectX 11 not supported' box in the DXMT mode, so this recipe runs it on D3DMetal. D3DMetal needs Apple's licence accepted once, under Graphics in the environment's settings.

knownIssues.cause: the launcher's embedded browser renders through DirectWrite, which paints nothing in this Wine (Sikarugir #255 has the same symptom for other CEF launchers)
knownIssues.fix: the registry step in this recipe, verified 2026-09-04: the launcher showed its EULA, updated the game and started it
knownIssues.symptom: The Warframe launcher window is black; the game never updates or starts

knownIssues.cause: the Steam account has no Warframe account linked yet; this is the game's own flow, not an engine problem
knownIssues.fix: choose Create New or Bind Existing in that dialog
knownIssues.symptom: 'Login with Steam' fails and a bind-or-create dialog appears

lastVerified.result: Launcher updated the game with the override, Steam login and account creation worked, the first tutorial mission ran under DXMT at about 35 fps and under DXVK at about 16 fps. Exit is clean.

steps.text: Warframe's Steam entry starts Tools\Launcher.exe, an updater with an embedded browser, and that browser paints nothing under this engine's DirectWrite (a black window with no buttons). The override above disables DirectWrite for Launcher.exe alone, so the launcher draws with GDI text, shows its EULA and Play button, and updates the game. The game keeps DirectWrite. Use DXMT for the game; DXVK runs it too but at about half the frame rate. The same per-executable override was described by leontov-eng on Sikarugir issue #255 on 2026-08-24; Highball ships it as data so nobody has to find winecfg.
